passage: Sunday afternoon in Jaya's rented room in Hyderabad, and nothing was due. She lay on the bed for ten minutes, then sat up, heart thumping. Lazy. She opened her laptop, closed it, reorganised her pens, and felt worse. Her friend Darshan, dropping off a borrowed book, found her pacing. 'You look like you're waiting for an exam result,' he said. 'I'm just wasting the day.' Darshan shrugged. 'Remember last month? You studied every single Sunday and fell asleep in the practical.' Jaya remembered. They walked to the lake, ate roasted corn and said nothing much. On Monday she finished her lab report in half the usual time and noticed, with surprise, that she didn't mind.

qa.q: What did Jaya and Darshan eat by the lake?
What was Jaya feeling when she lay on the bed with nothing due?
qa.a: She felt guilty and anxious, calling herself lazy, so the rest felt empty rather than restful.

qa.q: What helped Jaya see rest differently?
qa.a: Darshan reminded her that overwork had left her asleep in the practical, and after a real break she finished her report faster, showing rest improves later work.

qa.q: How did Darshan see Jaya's pacing?
qa.a: He saw that she was stressed, not resting, and gently reminded her of last month.

grounding: Shows a young adult who feels lazy and anxious whenever not being productive, and learns that genuine rest makes later work better.

passage:
The office had emptied when Arohi, his teammate, stopped at Jatin's desk.
'Jatin, it's nine. Why are you still here?'
'Just finishing the slides.'
'You finished them at six. I saw.'
'Then I'll check the numbers again.' Jatin rubbed his eyes. 'If I go home I'll just sit there feeling useless.'
'Useless how?'
'Last Sunday I watched a film and spent the whole time thinking I should be working. Couldn't enjoy a minute.'
'You know your best pitch was the week after Holi, when you'd taken four days off?'
'That was luck.'
'Was it? You were sharp. You laughed in meetings.'
Jatin went quiet. 'So rest is... part of the work?'
'It's what makes the work good. Go home. Take a walk. Leave the laptop shut.'
He saved the file and, slowly, closed it.

qa.q: When did Jatin actually finish the slides?
How did Jatin feel while watching a film last Sunday?
qa.a: He felt guilty and anxious, thinking he should be working, so he couldn't enjoy the rest.
Arohi reminded him that his best pitch came after four days off, helping him see rest as part of doing good work.

qa.q: How does Arohi see Jatin staying late?
qa.a: Arohi sees it as unnecessary and worrying, since the slides were done, and cares enough to send Jatin home.

grounding: Shows a young adult who feels useless and guilty whenever not working, and a teammate who helps him see that recovery makes later work better.
